goals: Explain PCA as finding directions of maximum variance
Choose the number of components with explained variance
Use PCA for compression and visualisation
why: PCA compresses many correlated features into a few, which speeds up models, removes noise and lets you plot high-dimensional data. It is used in finance (yield-curve factors), genomics and image processing.
explain: Photographing a teapot: some angles show its shape far better than others. PCA finds the **angle that shows the most variation** in your data, then the next best angle at right angles to it, and so on.
Each new axis is a **principal component**: a weighted combination of the original features. The first holds the most variance, the second the next most, and they are uncorrelated.
Keep enough components to explain, say, **90–95% of the variance** (check the cumulative explained-variance curve), and drop the rest as noise.
**Scale features first**, otherwise the feature with the biggest units dominates. Components are harder to interpret than the original features, so inspect the loadings to name them.

example.title: Compressing 20 survey questions
steps: Explained variance: PC1 48%, PC2 21%, PC3 9% → 78% in three
PC1 loads on all questions → "overall satisfaction"
PC2 contrasts price questions vs service questions → "value vs service"
example.result: Three interpretable scores replace 20 columns, ready for clustering or regression.

mistakes: Fitting PCA on all data before the split (leakage).
Assuming high-variance directions are the most predictive (not guaranteed).
takeaways: Rotate to the directions of maximum variance
Keep components up to ~90–95% explained variance
Scale first; components are combinations of features
avoid: When interpretability of the original features is required
interview: What do the eigenvalues represent in PCA?

practice.code:
from sklearn.datasets import load_breast_cancer
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
import numpy as np
X, _ = load_breast_cancer(return_X_y=True)
p = PCA().fit(StandardScaler().fit_transform(X))
cum = np.cumsum(p.explained_variance_ratio_)
print(cum[:6].round(3), "components for 95%:", int(np.argmax(cum >= 0.95)) + 1)
